finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: An attacker can provide a filename that includes shell metacharacters or special sequences to execute arbitrary commands.
finding.assumptions: The filename is directly used in the open function without any validation or sanitization.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked that svgFile.open(filename) uses std::ofstream::open, which opens a file directly without invoking a shell. No command execution occurs, so OS command injection is not possible.

finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: An attacker can provide SVG attributes that include shell metacharacters or special sequences to execute arbitrary commands.
finding.assumptions: The SVG attributes are directly written to the file without any validation or sanitization.

parsed.refutation_attempt: The reported sink is a stream insertion into an ofstream (svgFile). This operation merely writes bytes to a file; it does not invoke a shell or execute system commands. OS Command Injection requires that untrusted data be passed to a command interpreter (e.g., via system(), exec(), popen(), or similar). No such call exists in the fragment, and the only operations performed are string concatenations and stream writes. Therefore, there is no path from the untrusted inputs (fillColor, strokeColor, markerId, markerStart) to any command execution. The evidence lines 20, 24, 28, and 36 show only file output statements. No checks are needed because the vulnerability does not exist.
